lines.li: [them] So you're from the colony, then, family of a sort.
[us] I suppose we are, since the wedding.
[them,their:tribal] Then sit by me, family eats first.
[them,their:empire] A connection by marriage, yes, though not a close one.
[them] Then you'll forgive me for asking a lot of questions.
[them] How is {INLAW} getting on with you?
[us] Settling in, I'd say, more each week.
[us,tone:warm] Well, and nobody would send {INLAW} back now.
[them] Good, we worry, the way families do.
[us] How is {SPOUSEOF} doing among your people?
[them,their:tribal] Learning our songs, slowly, and our hunting, faster.
[them,their:medieval] Well liked at the market, and still lost at our festivals.
[them,their:industrial] Working hard, and already arguing with the neighbors.
[them,their:spacer] Adjusting, and asking a great many questions.
[them] Well enough, and asking after all of you.
[us] Tell {SPOUSEOF} we miss the noise.
[them] You're the one who married into all this, aren't you?
[us] I am, and I'm still learning everyone's names.
[them] Give it a year, then you'll know who to avoid.
[them] I have family here now, so I had to see the place for myself.
[us] And what do you make of it?
[them] Better than I feared, and I'll tell them so at home.
[them] You look well, the colony agrees with you.
[us] It does, though I miss home at harvest time.
[them] Home misses you too, I'm under orders to say so.
[us] How do your people hold a wedding?
[them,their:tribal] Gifts for the bride's family, and a fire the two of them share.
[them,their:medieval] Vows in the hall, a dowry counted out, and a long night.
[them,their:industrial] A wedding, a dinner, and papers signed before anyone gets drunk.
[them,their:spacer] A contract, witnessed and filed, and a quiet meal afterward.
[them,their:empire] By rank, with the titles read out, and nobody out of place.
[them] Much as you do, I expect, with more aunts.
[us] I'll remember that if we have another.
[them] People at home still talk about the wedding.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them,tone:warm] All good, and some of it is even true.
[them] Mostly good, and some of it about the food.
[them] A marriage ties two peoples better than any oath.
[us] An oath can be broken in a day.
[them,their:tribal] And a family can't, which is why the elders like it.
[them,their:spacer] Contracts lapse, families mostly don't.
[them] Exactly, which is why our head agreed to it.
[them] We heard you had raiders at your walls.
[us] We did, and we're still here.
[them] Next time, send word, family comes when family is in trouble.
[them] A marriage with your colony was much discussed at court.
[us] For or against?
[them] Both, at length, which at court means it was a success.
[us] Thank your people for the gifts they keep sending.
[them,their:tribal] It is how kin remember kin, each season, by the moons.
[them,their:medieval] It's custom, though my uncle grumbles about the cost.
[them,their:industrial] It's expected, and it keeps the road busy.
[them] It's what family does.
[them] Are you married too, then?
[us] I am, though nobody wrote a treaty about it.
[them] Then yours must be the happier one.
[them] Marriage or no marriage, I don't have to like you.
[us] No, you don't.
[them] Some at home still think the marriage was a mistake.
[us] And you?
[them] I think it's early days.
[them] I'm glad our people married into yours.
[us] So are we, and not only for the alliance.
[them] Good, then come and visit us one of these years.
[us] I'll hold you to that.
[them] How is the child?
[us] Growing, and asking about your people.
[them] Then we're still family, whatever else is gone.
[them] The child should learn our ways too, when they're older.
[them,their:tribal] Our songs, our hunting, the names of the elders.
[them,their:spacer] Our language, at least, and how we keep records.
[them] Our songs, at least, and where the family comes from.
[us] We'll see to it.
[them] So there's to be a wedding between our two peoples.
[us] There is, and it's all anyone asks me about.
[them,their:tribal] The gifts are already being made at home.
[them,their:medieval] The dowry is being counted out already.
[them,their:industrial] The arguments about the seating have started already.
[them] Ours too, but in a good way.
[us] What do your people think of {SPOUSEOF}?
[them] We only know what the letters say, and they say good things.
[us] And {INLAW}?
[them] {INLAW} is the one everyone at home will miss.
[them] Are they nervous, the two of them?
[us] I would be, in their place.
[them] So would I, and I'd still go through with it.
[them] We gave you one of ours, and you know what came of it.
[us] I wasn't the one who did it.
[them] Your colony was, and our people remember colonies, not names.
[them] At home the young ones are told what your colony did to one of us.
[us] Then I hope they're told we're sorry for it.
[them] They're told that too, and nobody believes it.
[them] Don't talk to me about marriages, not after what happened.
[us] Fair enough.
[them] When I lead my people, the grudge comes to me with the rest.
[us] Is there no way to set it down?
[them] Not one I've been told of.
[us] Has your family found you a match yet?
[them] They keep trying, and I keep finding reasons.
[them,their:empire] It must be someone of rank, which narrows things a great deal.
[them] Not yet, and I'm in no hurry.
[us] Well, if they look our way, I'll put in a word.
[us] Do your people marry for love, or for the family?
[them,their:tribal] For the clan, and love comes after, if it comes.
[them,their:medieval] For the house, mostly, and love is a lucky extra.
[them,their:industrial] For love, they say, and then they check the money.
[them,their:spacer] By contract, with clauses for when love runs out.
[them] Some of each, like everyone.
[them] My family asks about you in every letter now.
[us] What do you tell them?
[them] That they should ask your people properly, if they want to know more.
